summary: Casts a ray from each input point along a direction attribute against triangle or quad collision geometry in the second input. It can output hit distances, normals, reflected rays, far hits, hit counts, inside/outside state, primitive indices, barycentric coordinates, sampled attributes, projected points, or ray line strips.

key_concepts: Ray POP casts rays from input points along a named direction attribute against triangle or quad geometry in the second input.
Bounce, connect-points, trim, and length-limit controls can turn ray tests into projected points or explicit ray line strips.

Hit normals, reflection vectors, distances, far-hit state, hit counts, inside state, primitive indices, barycentric coordinates, and sampled hit attributes expose collision context for downstream POP logic.
common_gotchas: The second input must contain triangles or quads for collision testing.
Hardware ray tracing modes depend on GPU and geometry conditions; keep a non-hardware fallback path for portability.
Ray POP can project P by default; set scale and lift intentionally if you only want diagnostic attributes rather than moved points.
